metadata.title: Adaptive problem solving: Moving towards a new assessment domain in the second cycle of PIAAC

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD working paper is a conceptual and assessment-design document for the proposed second-cycle PIAAC domain of adaptive problem solving (APS), rather than an empirical analysis of PIAAC microdata. It therefore does not report an analytic sample, item response data, or any estimation procedure that would require applying PIAAC sampling weights or replicate weights. The paper discusses how APS could be assessed in a computer-based format (including the use of log-file indicators) and how background questionnaire (BQ) items could support interpretation, but it does not specify a weighting variable (e.g., TOTWGT or W_FSTUWT) or a replicate design (e.g., BRR/jackknife). For any future empirical implementation using PIAAC Data, analysts should apply the standard PIAAC complex survey design weights provided with the dataset when producing population-representative estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable here because the paper does not estimate cognitive achievement scales from PIAAC item responses; it instead develops a conceptual model and assessment principles for a new APS domain to be implemented in PIAAC 2. Missing-data handling is also not reported because there is no empirical dataset analysis, no analytic sample, and no model estimation pipeline described that would require specifying how missing responses were treated.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No student-level analytic sample is used. The paper provides a conceptual framework, covariates/preconditions, and assessment principles for the proposed APS domain in PIAAC 2, including example task designs and guidance for the background questionnaire.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Education Working Paper outlines the conceptual model and assessment design principles for adaptive problem solving (APS) to be assessed in the second cycle of PIAAC, alongside literacy and numeracy. It defines APS as a cognitive and metacognitive process occurring at the interface between internal processes and an external information environment, emphasizing monitoring and regulation as conditions for adaptivity. The paper proposes assessment principles for task development, including coverage of problem-solving processes, use of interactive/dynamic information-rich problems, and the role of computer-based administration and log-file indicators (e.g., response times, action sequences, and strategy indicators such as VOTAT). It also discusses how APS should relate to ICT literacy and how a PIAAC background questionnaire could capture covariates and precursors (e.g., literacy/numeracy, cognitive precursors, and non-cognitive factors). Because it is not an empirical ML study, it does not report model performance metrics or PV/missing-data handling results.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction contains many null/empty fields because the document is a framework and assessment-development paper rather than an empirical study using PIAAC microdata. It does not report an analytic sample, country-level Ns, PV estimation, missing-data procedures, or any ML model training/evaluation. Consequently, fields that depend on empirical estimation (e.g., plausible-value handling, missing-data handling strategy, ML techniques, and structured predictive findings) are not populated.
